mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent recessionary indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and starts to rise, it signals the beginning of a tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS rising from < 1% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decrease > 5% MoM does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, it signals a weak labor market with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: weak labor market with accommodative policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with subsequent economic recovery indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% month-over-month and industrial production (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average, it signals strong supply-side growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 10% MoM and INDPRO > 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion indicators.
